Definition: Ajin, the name (thus simply) of two places in Palestine
BiblicalUsage: Ain is the name of two towns in the south — one in Judah's inheritance and one in Simeon's — and of a place near Riblah on the northern border, where Joshua lists Ain among the cities and Numbers sets it on the boundary line of the land. The name means a spring or fountain, and the towns sat where water was.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God placed his towns by water on purpose, and I hold that the borders he drew for Israel were drawn with care — every spring counted, every town named.
